notes: Yihai Kerry Arawana Holdings (SZSE: 300999) — Wilmar International's China subsidiary, IPO'd on ChiNext in October 2020. China's largest cooking-oil/kitchen-foods company (Arawana brand) plus rice, flour, and feed-ingredient distribution. Reports CNY-millions PRC GAAP. Lists in CNY on Shenzhen ChiNext. FY ends Dec 31. Earnings highly sensitive to soybean/palm oil crush spreads — margins compressed FY22-FY24 on soft consumer demand and weaker oilseed-processing economics. Total debt figures pulled from balance sheet (short + long term interest-bearing). EBITDA reflects PRC reporting (operating profit + D&A); margin extremely thin given trader/processor business model.

periods.notes: FY20: First year as listed entity (IPO Oct 2020). Revenue RMB194.9bn, total profit >RMB6bn. Cooking oil + kitchen foods drove growth; pre-soybean-cost-spike year so margins remained healthy. Balance sheet detail not separately retrieved for this period.

FY21: Revenue RMB226.2bn (+16% YoY) on volume + price pass-through. EBITDA RMB10.1bn (margin 4.5%); NI RMB4.1bn (-31%) as soybean crush spreads compressed. Heavy working-capital build (commodity inventories) drove total debt to RMB93.7bn.

FY22: Revenue RMB257.5bn (+14%) on Russia/Ukraine driven oilseed price spike pass-through. EBITDA RMB7.5bn (margin 2.9%) — crush spreads turned negative for parts of year. NI RMB3.0bn (-27%). Net debt RMB70.6bn (+42% YoY) on commodity inventory.
FY23: Revenue RMB251.5bn (-2%) on softer ASP. EBITDA RMB4.9bn (margin 2.0%) — trough margin year as China consumer demand weakened. NI RMB2.85bn (-5%). Cash build to RMB59.3bn, net debt RMB56.6bn.

FY24: Revenue RMB238.3bn (-5%) on lower oilseed pricing. EBITDA RMB5.3bn (margin 2.2%); slight margin recovery. NI RMB2.5bn (-12%). Net debt RMB41.7bn (-26%) as inventory unwound. Wilmar parent retains ~89.99% stake.
